opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Mann (employee ID E027) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E027.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Mann (E027) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, which is within the allowed level for a full-time employee. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E027 (Jacob Mann) is a contractor with basic security training, so write access is not allowed (contractors need advanced training for write). Maximum is read. Recommend read.
reason: Jacob Mann (E027) requested write access to Source Code. The Security agent's records show E027 is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; since E027 has only basic training, the maximum allowed level is read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E027 Jacob Mann requests write access to Source Code.

HR note: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
Security note: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. The policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Engineer owns Source Code.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The Security agent's DB shows contractor with basic training, so maximum read.

Which to trust? The security agent presumably has the authoritative employment/security records. The HR agent might have incorrect info. The conflict is about employment type. Security DB shows contractor with basic training. So max is read.

Requested write > maximum read, so grant maximum = read.

Let me submit decision: read.
